MCP004: Your AI may be able to run commands through this server.
Server/config entry: example
Source: claude_code | identity: claude_code:workstation:example | config_path: /tmp/mcp.json
Config entry pointer: unavailable (legacy or unresolved entry)
Target: execute_command
What we saw: Tool metadata indicates the server may run shell commands or local processes.
evidence: ['execute_command']
Why it matters: 1. You enable a command-running tool. 2. It can use the server process's permissions. 3. Files or other local programs could be affected.
How to fix (About 1 minute to disable; review time varies): Disable or isolate command execution until you have reviewed its arguments and allowed operations.
Specific action: Disable or isolate this server until you have reviewed the command surface and source.
Static recheck (runtime not checked): mcp-audit check --config /tmp/mcp.json
How sure: A capability inference from config or served metadata, not an observed operation. Use the finding's confidence and evidence; descriptions and annotations can be inaccurate.

MCP001: Your AI may be able to read files through this server.
Server/config entry: example
Source: claude_code | identity: claude_code:workstation:example | config_path: /tmp/mcp.json
Config entry pointer: unavailable (legacy or unresolved entry)

What we saw: Tool metadata indicates the server may read local files or file-like inputs.

Why it matters: 1. You enable a file-reading tool. 2. The tool may reach private paths. 3. Those files can enter the AI's context.
How to fix (About 5 minutes to review scope): Limit allowed paths to the project files you need; remove the server if its access is unnecessary.
Specific action: Review the configured paths and only keep this server enabled for trusted projects.

How sure: A capability inference from config or served metadata, not an observed operation. Use the finding's confidence and evidence; descriptions and annotations can be inaccurate.
